nodes.name: GSA AG / Gewinde Ziegler AG
nodes.description: Swiss planetary/satellite roller-screw specialist (Gewinde Satelliten Antriebe AG / Gewinde Ziegler AG, est. 1982). Makes the RGTI inverted planetary roller screw widely reported as the type Tesla sources for Optimus linear actuators; modeled as a near-single-source roller-screw supplier candidate for the humanoid linear-joint stack. Privately held.

nodes.name: Rollvis SA
nodes.description: Swiss (Geneva, est. 1970) satellite/planetary roller-screw specialist trading as 'Rollvis Swiss'; self-described world leader in satellite roller screws. Together with GSA, frequently cited as holding the majority of the high-precision planetary roller-screw world market — the Swiss near-single-source corner feeding humanoid linear actuators. Privately held.

nodes.name: Thread-grinding / ultra-precision CNC grinding equipment
nodes.description: Ultra-precision CNC thread-grinding machines that cut the sub-3-micron-tolerance internal and external threads of planetary roller screws (and ball screws). This is the upstream capital-equipment bottleneck behind the Swiss roller-screw corner: the specialized internal-thread grinding expertise and the thin population of qualified grinder builders gate how fast roller-screw capacity can be added for humanoid linear actuators.

nodes.name: Drake Manufacturing Services
nodes.description: US (Warren, Ohio) builder of precision CNC thread- and gear-grinding machines, including internal thread grinders and ball-nut/ballscrew grinders for the ball-screw and linear-motion industries — the upstream grinding-equipment tier behind roller/ball-screw production. Privately held.

nodes.name: PTG Holroyd
nodes.description: UK builder of high-precision gear, rotor, screw and thread milling and grinding machines, marketed as producing the world's most accurate helical components — part of the thin population of ultra-precision thread/screw grinder builders upstream of roller-screw production. Part of the Precision Technologies Group; privately held.

nodes.name: Shenzhen PICEA Motion (formerly Han's Motion)
nodes.description: Shenzhen-based precision harmonic-drive / strain-wave reducer maker, formerly Shenzhen Han's Motion Technology Co., Ltd., rebranded to PICEA Motion. Cited among the global key manufacturers of humanoid-robot harmonic reducers and a Chinese domestic-substitution alternative to Harmonic Drive/Nabtesco. Privately held (some trade sources describe it as a former Han's Laser subsidiary; the company's own site presents it independently).

nodes.name: JL MAG Rare-Earth
nodes.description: Dual-listed (Shenzhen 300748.SZ / Hong Kong 06680.HK) Chinese sintered-NdFeB permanent-magnet maker; in 2025 upgraded its humanoid-robot magnetic-component R&D department to a dedicated business unit. Magnet output sits inside China's rare-earth export-licensing regime. Component-exposure candidate; not a confirmed humanoid BOM placement.

nodes.name: Shin-Etsu Chemical
nodes.description: Public Tokyo-listed (4063.T) maker of NdFeB (Nd-Fe-B) sintered rare-earth magnets (N Series) used in industrial servomotors and linear motors; operates Japan's large-scale rare-earth separation/refining and is building a heavy-rare-earth refinery to diversify supply off China. Component-exposure candidate; not a confirmed humanoid BOM placement.

nodes.name: Proterial
nodes.description: Private Japanese magnet/materials maker (ex-Hitachi Metals; renamed 2023 after a Bain Capital-led buyout) that pioneered and mass-produces NEOMAX Nd-Fe-B sintered magnets for motors, and mass-produces a heavy-rare-earth-saving grade that minimizes dysprosium/terbium. PRIVATE — no public ticker. Component-exposure candidate; not a confirmed humanoid BOM placement.

nodes.name: Regal Rexnord
nodes.description: Public NYSE-listed (RRX) motion-control group whose brands include Kollmorgen (and Portescap, acquired via the 2023 Altra deal). Kollmorgen frameless / direct-drive torque motors (TBM/KBM/TBM2G) target robot, cobot and humanoid joints. Component-exposure candidate; not a confirmed humanoid BOM placement.

nodes.name: maxon
nodes.description: Private Swiss precision-drive maker; its EC frameless DT torque motors and integrated High Efficiency Joint (HEJ) actuators explicitly target humanoids, quadrupeds and exoskeletons. (Also a hollow-cup/coreless micromotor specialist for dexterous hands.) PRIVATE — no public ticker. Component-exposure candidate; not a confirmed humanoid BOM placement.

nodes.name: Netzer Precision
nodes.description: Private Israeli maker of contactless capacitive (Electric Encoder) absolute hollow-shaft encoders; immune to magnetic interference near frameless-motor magnets, used in humanoid/space robot arm joints (e.g. NASA Robonaut 2). Supplier candidate.

nodes.name: Novanta (ATI Industrial Automation)
nodes.description: US NASDAQ-listed precision-technology group; its ATI Industrial Automation division is a long-incumbent maker of multi-axis (six-axis) force/torque sensors for robotic force control, a supplier candidate for humanoid wrist/hand force-torque sensing.

nodes.name: Bota Systems
nodes.description: Private Swiss (Zurich) maker of compact 6-axis force/torque sensors, torque sensors and tactile sensors for humanoid, medical and collaborative robots (MiniONE, PixONE). Supplier candidate for humanoid force-torque / fingertip sensing.

nodes.name: Sunrise Instruments (SRI)
nodes.description: Privately-held six-axis force/torque sensor and multi-axis load-cell maker (HQ Canton, Michigan, US; manufacturing in China) with a dedicated humanoid-robot 6-axis force/torque sensor line (C025XX-C060XX). Supplier candidate.

nodes.name: XELA Robotics
nodes.description: Private (Waseda University spin-out, Tokyo) maker of uSkin high-density three-axis tactile skin sensors covering fingertips, phalanges and palm for humanoid and industrial robot hands/grippers. Supplier candidate for humanoid tactile sensing.

nodes.name: PaXini Technology
nodes.description: Private Chinese maker of multidimensional tactile sensors (PX-6AX series, Hall-effect 6D force/torque) and tactile dexterous hands (DexH13) for humanoid / embodied-AI robots; full-stack tactile + hand + robot supplier candidate.

nodes.name: Bosch Sensortec
nodes.description: MEMS sensor subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH (private); high-performance IMUs (BMI088, BMI323, BMI563) explicitly targeted at robotics incl. agile humanoid and social robots. Supplier candidate for humanoid IMU/attitude sensing.

nodes.name: Hesai Group
nodes.description: Chinese LiDAR maker, dual-listed Nasdaq (HSAI) / HKEX (2525); JT-series mini 360° 3D robotics LiDAR for mobile/humanoid robots; named only LiDAR firm on Morgan Stanley's Humanoid Tech 25. Supplier candidate for humanoid depth/LiDAR perception.

nodes.name: RoboSense Technology
nodes.description: Chinese LiDAR / robotic-vision maker, HKEX-listed (2498.HK); Active Camera (AC1/AC2) fused LiDAR+RGB+IMU vision and dexterous hands for humanoid robots; partnerships with multiple humanoid firms. Supplier candidate for humanoid perception.

nodes.name: Orbbec
nodes.description: Chinese 3D-vision camera maker, Shanghai STAR-listed (688322.SS); Gemini-series stereo-vision depth cameras for robotics/embodied AI (HONOR humanoid, Reachy 2; Jetson Thor integration); reported >70% 3D-vision share in China service robots / Korea mobile robots. Supplier candidate.

nodes.name: RealSense Inc.
nodes.description: Stereo depth-camera maker spun out of Intel into a standalone private company (2025; ~$50M Series A, NVIDIA collaboration). D4xx depth cameras (e.g. D455 in Agility Digit's neck); reports working with ~60% of AMR and humanoid developers. Supplier candidate for humanoid depth/RGB perception.

nodes.name: EVE Energy
nodes.description: Public Shenzhen-listed (ChiNext) lithium-ion and all-solid-state battery cell maker; ticker 300014.SZ is mainland China A-share exposure, not a US primary listing. Cell-merchant supplier candidate; humanoid packs remain integrator-captive.

nodes.name: Molicel (E-One Moli Energy)
nodes.description: Ultra-high-power cylindrical lithium-ion cell maker; merchant cell supplier candidate listing 'humanoid robotics applications' on its product site. Not directly listed; ticker 1101.TW is its parent Taiwan Cement Corporation (TCC) Group on the Taiwan Stock Exchange, i.e. indirect parent-level exposure, not a US primary listing. Humanoid packs remain integrator-captive; Molicel supplies cells.

nodes.name: Panasonic (Panasonic Energy / Panasonic Holdings)
nodes.description: Major high-power/high-energy cylindrical lithium-ion cell maker (2170 format). Merchant cell supplier candidate; ticker 6752.T is the parent Panasonic Holdings on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (Panasonic Energy is its battery segment), i.e. Japan-listed exposure, not a US primary listing. Humanoids repurpose this high-power cylindrical cell class; packs remain integrator-captive.

nodes.name: Infineon Technologies
nodes.description: Public power-semiconductor and microcontroller maker (power switches/MOSFETs, gate drivers, battery-monitoring & balancing ICs, MCUs). Merchant-silicon supplier for humanoid power electronics / BMS front-ends; ticker IFX.DE is Frankfurt/Xetra exposure (US OTC: IFNNY), not a US primary listing. Supplies the merchant ICs; the BMS control firmware/algorithm is the robot maker's (captive).

nodes.name: NXP Semiconductors
nodes.description: Public NASDAQ-listed (NXPI) semiconductor maker; supplies battery-management ICs and standalone BMS reference designs aimed at mobile robotics (drones/rovers), plus MCUs for BMS/inverter use. Merchant-silicon supplier candidate; the pack BMS firmware/integration remains the robot maker's.

nodes.name: Qualcomm
nodes.description: Public US-listed (Nasdaq) robotics SoC supplier; markets the Dragonwing IQ10 series premium-tier onboard 'brain of the robot' processor for full-size humanoids and AMRs, and is collaborating with Figure on humanoid compute architecture. Merchant alternative to NVIDIA Jetson Thor for onboard AI compute.

nodes.name: NXP Semiconductors
nodes.description: Public US-listed (Nasdaq) semiconductor supplier; provides i.MX 95 applications processor (machine-vision edge node) and i.MX RT1180 crossover MCUs aggregated by an S32J TSN switch for humanoid motor control, developed with NVIDIA as distributed edge-perception/motor-control complements to the central robot brain. Spans onboard compute SoC and real-time motor-control MCU components.

nodes.name: Fuzhou Rockchip Electronics
nodes.description: Public China-listed (Shanghai) application-processor SoC designer; its RK3588/RK3588S edge SoC (octa-core, ~6 TOPS NPU) is the adopted main compute/'brain' platform in multiple Chinese humanoid robots (e.g. AgiBot/ZhiYuan Lingxi X2, LimX Oli). Low-cost merchant onboard-compute alternative to NVIDIA Jetson Thor for domestic humanoids.

nodes.name: D-Robotics
nodes.description: Privately held robot-chip spinoff of Horizon Robotics (HKEX: 9660; D-Robotics shares a technological lineage and coordinated roadmaps with it but is a separate, Series-A-funded company). Makes the RDK S100 — the industry's first single-SoC platform integrating robot 'brain' (compute) and 'cerebellum' (control), 80-128 TOPS — for developers of humanoid robots. Merchant onboard compute-control SoC.

nodes.name: Infineon Technologies
nodes.description: Public Germany-listed (Frankfurt) power-semiconductor and MCU supplier; for humanoid motor control provides gate drivers, current sensors, a GaN-based motor-control chip set, and PSOC Control C3 MCUs (FOC, EtherCAT) that pair with NVIDIA Jetson Thor via Holoscan Sensor Bridge (Aug 2025 NVIDIA collaboration). Merchant motor-drive power-electronics and real-time MCU supplier.

nodes.name: Efficient Power Conversion (EPC)
nodes.description: Privately held (El Segundo, CA) gallium-nitride (GaN) power-semiconductor maker; offers the EPC91122 3-phase BLDC motor-drive inverter evaluation board engineered specifically for humanoid robot joint applications, plus GaN parts for compact wrist/finger/toe motors. Merchant GaN motor-drive/gate-driver-inverter supplier for humanoid actuators.

nodes.name: Microchip Technology
nodes.description: Public US-listed (Nasdaq) microcontroller and analog supplier; its dsPIC33 DSC-based integrated motor drivers combine a digital signal controller, a three-phase MOSFET gate driver, and LIN/CAN FD into one device for FOC BLDC/PMSM motor control. Merchant motor-drive MCU + gate-driver supplier applicable to humanoid joint/actuator drive (robotics/industrial motor-control class, humanoid design win not yet confirmed).

nodes.name: Victrex
nodes.description: Public London-listed PEEK polymer maker (VICTREX PEEK / PAEK, HPG gears); one of ~4 thousand-ton-scale PEEK producers worldwide. Markets PEEK for robotics gears, bushings/bearings, and lightweight components replacing metal. PEEK is the headline lightweighting polymer in humanoid skeletons/limbs.

nodes.name: Evonik
nodes.description: Public Frankfurt-listed specialty-chemicals maker; VESTAKEEP PEEK line (incl. tribological Easy Slide 2 slide bearings) explicitly marketed to the robotics industry. One of ~4 thousand-ton-scale PEEK producers worldwide.

nodes.name: Zhejiang Sanhua Intelligent Controls

CAUTION: a quality source states Sanhua's current humanoid focus is electromechanical actuators, not thermal systems — the 'exclusive Optimus liquid-cooling supplier' claims trace to SEO/substack and are NOT confirmed here. Modeled reported-capable; flag for verifier.

evidence.title: Harmonic Drive capacity increase — Ariake Plant
evidence.summary: Harmonic Drive discloses that strain-wave gearing capacity is raised only in large fixed increments gated by a multi-year capital project (150k to 220k units/month), illustrating that precision strain-wave supply cannot scale quickly as humanoid joint demand surges. Supports the near-single-source/capacity-gating corner on the strain-wave reducer.
evidence.limitations: Capacity figure is for all strain-wave applications (industrial robots, semiconductor equipment, automotive), not humanoid-specific; does not by itself prove market share. Used as qualitative capacity-gating evidence.
evidence.excerpt: The capital investment will enable the Ariake Plant (Nagano Prefecture) to increase production capacity of Harmonic Drive® strain wave gearing devices from 150,000 units/month to 220,000 units/month by August 2022.

evidence.title: Highly Developed Humanoid Robots — Nidec Drive Technology
evidence.summary: Nidec Drive Technology markets its Next Generation FLEXWAVE strain-wave gear reducers as the ideal choice for humanoid-robot joint positioning, confirming Nidec as a merchant strain-wave reducer supplier candidate for the humanoid joint stack.
evidence.limitations: Vendor application page; supports FLEXWAVE strain-wave reducers as marketed for humanoid joints (reducer exposure), not a confirmed humanoid customer, share, or qualification.
evidence.excerpt: The Next Generation Nidec FLEXWAVE high precision simple contained assembly and component sub-assembly gear reducers are the ideal choice for these types of applications.

evidence.title: RGTI: Inverted Planetary Roller Screw — GSA
evidence.summary: GSA's RGTI inverted planetary roller screw is described as a high-load, high-positioning-accuracy electromechanical drive integrated in hollow-shaft motors — the configuration used in humanoid linear actuators. Supports GSA as a planetary-roller-screw supplier candidate for the humanoid linear-joint stack.
evidence.limitations: Vendor product page; supports the RGTI roller-screw design and hollow-shaft-motor integration. Does not itself confirm the Tesla Optimus contract, volumes, or market share.
evidence.excerpt: The RGTI is mainly integrated as an electromechanical drive in hollow shaft motors. It offers a compact electromechanical alternative to hydraulic and pneumatic lifting and linear drives.

evidence.title: GSA — Planetary Roller Screws (company)
evidence.summary: GSA states all roller-screw components are manufactured and assembled in-house at GSA AG / Gewinde Ziegler AG (Switzerland), confirming a vertically integrated Swiss roller-screw specialist — one of the two firms behind the Swiss concentration of high-precision planetary roller screws.
evidence.limitations: Establishes Swiss in-house manufacturing and company identity; does not quantify share. The >50% combined Swiss share is carried qualitatively in the roller-screw corner note.
evidence.excerpt: All components are manufactured and assembled in-house at GSA AG / Gewinde Ziegler AG.

evidence.title: Rollvis SA — About Us
evidence.summary: Rollvis SA (Geneva, founded 1970) self-describes as a world leader in the design and production of satellite roller screws for high-precision linear motion — one of the two Swiss firms behind the concentration of high-precision planetary roller-screw supply for humanoid linear actuators.
evidence.limitations: Vendor about-page; establishes Swiss world-leader identity and roller-screw specialism, not a specific humanoid customer or quantified share.
evidence.excerpt: ROLLVIS SA is a world leader in the design and production of Satellite Roller screws.

evidence.title: China's grip on the humanoid robot future — roller-screw supply
evidence.summary: Reports that planetary-roller-screw adoption is constrained by limited supply and high production cost rooted in the specialized manufacturing expertise required — the binding scarcity constraint on humanoid linear-actuator scale-up. Supports the single/near-single-source corner on the roller-screw component.
evidence.limitations: Trade-press synthesis, not a primary capacity disclosure; qualitative scarcity/expertise claim, no single firm's share quantified.
evidence.excerpt: Currently, both ball and planetary roller screws are used for humanoids, but this is largely due to the limited supply and cost of planetary roller screws ... the widespread adoption of planetary roller screws has been constrained by their high production cost, which can be primarily attributed to the specialized manufacturing expertise required

evidence.title: Triton completes sale of Ewellix to Schaeffler AG
evidence.summary: Confirms Ewellix — a global manufacturer of linear motion and actuation solutions (incl. roller screws) — is now owned by Schaeffler AG (sale completed 2023). This is why humanoid roller-screw exposure via Ewellix maps to org_schaeffler, the same group already flagged as a >50% preferred actuator supplier.
evidence.limitations: Confirms ownership and that Ewellix makes linear motion/actuation solutions; does not by itself quantify roller-screw share or a humanoid customer.
evidence.excerpt: Triton Fund V advised by Triton Partners ("Triton"), has completed the sale of Ewellix ("Ewellix"), a global innovator and manufacturer of linear motion and actuation solutions, to Schaeffler AG
